en: I always worship Rāma, who has the luster of a blue lotus, who is described as a forest fire to the jungle of worldly existence, whose form is bliss realized by the heart of Bhavānī, who is the cause of the cessation of worldly existence, and who is the refuge of those like Bhava. || 1 ||

I worship Hari, Rāma, the Lord who destroys the burden [of worldly existence], the supreme master whose form is the highest bliss, the most excellent one worthy of praise, the formless being who assumes a human body as the sole cause for destroying the flood of suffering of the army of demons.

I worship Rāmamitra, who grants the bliss of all who have sought refuge, who is himself a seeker of refuge, whose name signifies the total destruction of the suffering of those surrendered to him, who is to be realized through the state of a master yogi of austerity and yoga, and who has the lord of monkeys and others as his friends.

I take refuge in the Lord Rāghava, the root of consciousness and bliss, who shines ever far away from those devoted to worldly enjoyments, yet shines ever near to those devoted to yoga; he who is the very embodiment of the joy of the daughter of Videha. || 4 ||
O Lord, you who shine forth through your engagement with the extraordinary power of great yoga, manifesting in the form of a playful human being—
those whose ears are filled with the stories of your blissful pastimes become embodiments of eternal bliss in this world.
Formerly, intoxicated by the pride of being the lord of all, I was heedless through the intoxication of my own conceit;
now, by the grace of your lotus feet, that pride of sovereignty over the three worlds has perished.

I worship the Lord Rāghava, who is beautiful with shimmering jeweled armlets and necklaces; who is a forest fire to the hosts of asuras who constitute the burden of the earth; whose face is like the autumn moon and whose lotus-eyes gleam; and whose further shore is difficult to reach.

I worship Rāmacandra, the sovereign of the Raghus, whose body possesses the luster of a dark cloud belonging to the lord of the gods; who brings peace to the world through the slaying of demons such as Virādha; who is adorned with a crown and other ornaments; and who attained the status of the enemy of Tripura.

I worship Rāmacandra, who has dispelled all suffering and lethargy, seated upon a throne radiant as ten million moons, holding Sītā on his lap— she who is of shimmering golden hue and possesses the brilliance of a mass of lightning.
Thus ends the hymn to Śrī Rāma composed by Indra, in the thirteenth sarga of the Yuddhakāṇḍa of the glorious Adhyātmarāmāyaṇa.
